paginas.texto: Agenda Cádiz Ir al contenido principal La Agenda informa. La crónica cuenta. Y Cádiz se siente. Agenda Cádiz nace con el deseo de iluminar todo aquello que construye nuestra ciudad. Cádiz no es solo calles, historia o mar. Es su gente, sus artistas, sus escenarios, sus deportistas, sus barrios y sus iniciativas. Agenda Cádiz quiere ser tu ventana abierta a todo lo que ocurre aquí, informando y emocionando con cada historia. Te invitamos a "Cádiz desde sus Barrios", conectando con el alma de Cádiz. Únete a nosotros para explorar las historias que dan vida a nuestra tierra. Pasa… la ciudad tiene algo que contarte. Desde eventos culturales hasta noticias locales, te acercamos lo mejor de Cádiz. Nuestro objetivo es que no te pierdas nada de lo que acontece en nuestra maravillosa ciudad. Sumérgete en nuestras secciones y vive Cádiz como nunca antes. Arte y Cultura Descubre los eventos culturales, exposiciones y actuaciones que hacen vibrar a Cádiz. Desde flamenco hasta teatro, el arte local te espera. Ver eventos Deporte y Ocio Mantente al día con las últimas noticias deportivas y las actividades de ocio para todos los gustos en la provincia. Ver noticias Cádiz desde sus Barrios Las historias que dan vida a cada rincón de nuestros barrios gaditanos. Explorar proyectos Sociedad Porque una ciudad también se cuenta desde sus personas Leer más Sobre Agenda Cádiz Agenda Cádiz nace desde una mirada sencilla pero profundamente necesaria: la de contar la ciudad que late cada día. Somos un espacio para informar, emocionar, descubrir y acompañar. Creemos que una ciudad se construye narrando sus historias y capturando el alma de lo que sucede. Historias contadas en píxeles Aquí encontrarás galerías y reportajes fotográficos que capturan la esencia de Cádiz. Desde la emoción de un teatro lleno hasta la verdad de un artista callejero, cada imagen cuenta una parte de nuestra historia. "Agenda Cádiz me ha permitido descubrir eventos increíbles en mi propia ciudad que de otra forma me hubiera perdido. ¡Es una fuente inagotable de información!" María R. "Gracias a esta plataforma, siempre estoy al tanto de las últimas noticias y las iniciativas solidarias de mi barrio. Es un gran recurso para la comunidad." Javier S. "La forma en que Agenda Cádiz captura el espíritu de la ciudad es única. No solo informa, sino que te hace sentir parte de ella." Carmen P. "Lo que más valoro de Agenda Cádiz es que habla de la ciudad desde las personas. Su mirada social e inclusiva marca la diferencia." — Antonio R. "Cada historia demuestra que una ciudad se construye con cultura, pero también con empatía e inclusión. Gracias por hacerlo visible." — Carmen L. Clarent | Urbana, Trap, Latina Fecha: domingo 22 de noviembre de 2026 Sala: Montera Forum, Los Barrios Localidad: Cádiz Hora: 21:00 h. Precio Entradas: Información: Clarent: Presenta el disco "No Pasa Nada Hombre" El artista puertorriqueño de música urbana Clarent actúa dentro de su nueva gira a la que bautizado " No Pasa Nada Hombre Tour " y que se basa en su primer disco de estudio que da nombre al tour. El álbum reúne reggaetón, trap, R&B, pop, electrónica y rock y cuenta con destacadas colaboraciones de Quevedo , Omar Courtz , Wisin, Tainy, Mora , De La Rose , Yovngchimi y Cris MJ. "No Pasa Nada Hombre" vio la luz el 1 de octubre de 2026 con 18 cortes. Llega tras " No Vuelve a Suceder ", un "pre-calientamiento" del nuevo disco que salió editado en enero de 2026. Clarent cuenta con más de siete millones de escuchas mensuales en Spotify, gracias sobretodo al single " IA "; colaboración con Mora . ¿Conoces a Clarent y su directo? Conversations About Relationships Online event Link visible for attendees Event chat Attend to join the conversation and connect with other attendees before the event starts Attend event Event chat Attend to join the conversation and connect with other attendees before the event starts Attend event The 8 Strategies That Run Your Relationships Hosted by Mila S. Conversations About Relationships Details We all have a handful of automatic moves we make in close relationships. They fire faster than thought. They feel like personality rather than choice. From the inside, you cannot see your own strategy. In this session I will walk you through all eight, one by one. Most people recognise themselves in three. What we'll do Eight strategies, described from the inside, as the sentences that actually run through your head daily. For each one: what it sounds like internally, what the person next to you experiences, and the trap that keeps it in place. And at the end, the uncomfortable finding: the strategy you recognised is the one you already knew about. Your strongest one is almost certainly among the ones you did not pick — and there is a structural reason you cannot find it alone. Who this is for People in long relationships where something has gone flat. People who left one relationship and keep meeting the same dynamic in the next. People who have done therapy, understand their patterns intellectually, and notice that every evening still goes the way it always did. You do not need any background in psychology. What you'll leave with Names for three things you have been doing for years without a name. One small experiment to run this week. And a clear picture of where your blind spot sits. About me I'm Mila Skalkina, a psychologist and life coach. I work with couples and run therapy groups. I've lived in Russia, Zimbabwe, the Netherlands and now Spain, which taught me more about losing and rebuilding yourself than any textbook did. These eight strategies did not come from a manual. They came from my own work, from the things people actually say about themselves when nobody is performing. Details Online, 60 minutes, free. Come with a notebook, leave the camera off if you prefer. candidatos.detalle_texto: Software Engineering: Extinction or Evolution?, Thu, Nov 5, 2026, 5:30 PM | Meetup Skip to content Software Engineering: Extinction or Evolution? Hosted by SGI Super Organizer Beyond the Code This is a hybrid event Thursday, Nov 5 · 5:30 PM to 9:00 PM GMT The Loading Bay - at Techspace The Loading Bay, Clifton St, London EC2A 4HT, UK · London Online event Link visible for attendees Software Engineering: Extinction or Evolution? Hosted by SGI Super Organizer Beyond the Code Details AI is changing software engineering at a pace that is difficult to ignore, but how much has actually changed, and what does it mean for the people building software today? Beyond the Code’s first live panel brings together an elite panel of experts for a candid discussion about what AI is genuinely changing on the ground, what is still hype, and what the future could mean for engineering teams and individual careers. The panel will be split into two distinct halves: What’s Actually Changed? AI coding tools, copilots, agents and increasingly capable models are already changing how software is built. But beyond the headlines, what does that look like in practice? Betting on What Survives. Looking beyond the current wave of AI adoption, what might software engineering look like in the years ahead, and how should people prepare for it? The aim is not to predict the future with certainty, but to have a frank, practical conversation about the signals worth watching and what engineers and organisations can do about them. Whether you're building software, leading engineering teams, hiring technical talent or thinking about where your own career goes next, this event will offer a practical look at what AI is really changing and what may be next. candidatos.detalle_texto: Monthly Tarot Practice Group: Check in With Your Deck, Sun, Nov 1, 2026, 2:00 PM | Meetup Skip to content Monthly Tarot Practice Group: Check in With Your Deck Hosted by Maria Super Organizer Fortune Minding with Maria Every 1st Sunday of the month until December 12, 2026 Online event Link visible for attendees Monthly Tarot Practice Group: Check in With Your Deck Hosted by Maria Super Organizer Fortune Minding with Maria Details This relaxed and informative (and FREE!) session will give you the chance to check in on your tarot journey as well as pick up a few new strategies and techniques to incorporate into your practice. Every month we will be working from a different topic, idea, question, spread, etc. Feel free to join every month, or pop in as you wish. A few things to know: This session is open to all levels of experience, but complete beginners should know that this session is hands-on and we will not be teaching you how to read tarot. However, you are more than welcome to attend, and we will explain how to engage with your cards on an intuitive level even if you've never studied tarot before. (If you are looking for a class, though, get in touch! I do offer a beginner's course, which runs at various points during the year) Most of us (myself included) tend to work from the Rider-Waite-Smith tarot and decks that are RWS-inspired. You are encouraged to bring any deck you feel drawn to, but (especially if you're a beginner) it's usually better to have a deck with unique images on each card. For that reason, I would suggest using Marseille & Thoth-based tarot decks only if you are already confident in that system. # **How to build an AI QA process that saves the most – and uses human time only where it counts?**

AI doesn't wait for a bug report. In AI-native QA teams, the agent doesn't just run tests – it writes them, mai
candidatos.detalle_texto: How to trust an AI-driven QA process | Product Builders | AI-Native #5, Thu, Nov 5, 2026, 4:00 PM | Meetup Skip to content How to trust an AI-driven QA process | Product Builders | AI-Native #5 Hosted by Boldare Product Builders | AI-Native: Live Sessions, Real Work Online event Link visible for attendees Event chat Attend to join the conversation and connect with other attendees before the event starts Attend event Event chat Attend to join the conversation and connect with other attendees before the event starts Attend event How to trust an AI-driven QA process | Product Builders | AI-Native #5 Hosted by Boldare Product Builders | AI-Native: Live Sessions, Real Work Details REGISTER HERE # How to build an AI QA process that saves the most – and uses human time only where it counts? AI doesn't wait for a bug report. In AI-native QA teams, the agent doesn't just run tests – it writes them, maintains them, reacts to code changes, and decides what still needs checking. The catch: code is still the final judge of quality – except now the code is asking itself whether it did a good job. In this Product Builders | AI-Native session , Piotr Majchrzak (co-CEO, Boldare) and Milena Cylinska (QA Lead & Test Automation Engineer) show how to build a QA process where a human still knows what to trust and what not to – even when AI handles most of the testing. You'll learn: how to spot that "all tests passed" can be a false sense of security rather than proof of quality, exactly where to place checkpoints in QA automation so AI never grades its own work unsupervised, how to design a system that earns more autonomy over time – starting small and expanding only based on data, not declarations. Coming from a team running this in production, the session skips the theory and gets straight to what actually works: a testing process you can trust, and know exactly why. About Product Builders | AI Native Product Builders | AI-Native is a community for practitioners building digital products in the AI era – Substack is where it all comes together.
